clue.text: "Funny girl" author drops by to get instrument

parts.note: the comedian Dawn French is a famous funny woman, giving her surname

indicators.note: the author's name lets go of the following word, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: Nick Hornby is the author of High Fidelity and Fever Pitch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist whose book is called Funny Girl pays a visit to pick up a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny girl' reads as a book title in quotes, but it is the comic Dawn French; 'drops by' is not a visit but HORNBY losing BY to leave HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: This coiled brass wind piece is a standard orchestral instrument.

clue.text: Passenger's diet

definitions.meaning: a paying customer in a taxi
the food a person eats, as in plain country food

explanation.definitionFit: A cab driver's paying rider, and the food served or eaten.

clue.text: Enlighten English earl about old gold coin

indicators.note: the two single letters go around the coin, one on each side

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earl in the peerage
a ducat was a gold coin used across Europe in past centuries

explanation.surface: An English nobleman explains an antique gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Es 'about' DUCAT go one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to teach or inform them.

clue.text: Farm tea prepared with carrot cake baked with this?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A farmhouse tea is prepared with a carrot cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges FARM TEA and CARROT together; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: This white powder, potassium bitartrate, is a raising agent used in baking.

clue.text: Dance with goddess round a bar

indicators.note: the goddess's name wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
to bar is to ban or forbid

explanation.surface: Someone dances with a goddess around a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a verb here, BAN, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A habanera is a slow Cuban dance in duple time, famous from Carmen.

clue.text: American wines found outside studies

indicators.note: the wines are placed on the outside of the other letter

parts.note: reds are red wines

explanation.surface: Some American wines are found outside on a terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studies' is a verb, as in poring over books.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a book is to peruse it, so studies works as a synonym.

clue.text: Reptile caught huge bird

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the roc is the giant mythical bird of the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A reptile snaps up an enormous bird.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'caught' is a cricket scoring convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal name for a crocodile, a large reptile.

clue.text: Denied judge trained duet

parts.note: a referee judges a match, abbreviated ref

indicators.note: trained, as in drilled or reshaped, signals the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge has rejected a trained singing duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges DUET to UTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a claim is to rebut it, prove it false.

clue.text: Disinfect rotten old clarinet with bleach at the end

indicators.note: rotten, like something gone bad, signals the letters are rearranged
only the final letter of the word bleach is used

explanation.surface: A musician disinfects a rotten old clarinet, finishing off with bleach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' shuffles O, CLARINET and H, the letter 'at the end' of bleach.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinfect water or a pool is to treat it with a chemical sterilant, which is this.

clue.text: Rake round end of dirt track

indicators.note: the word for rake goes round the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roue

indicators.note: the final letter of the word dirt is the one taken

explanation.surface: A garden rake is dragged around the far end of a muddy path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool but is the old word for a libertine; ROUE goes 'round' T, the last letter of 'dirt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a way or path taken, a synonym of a road or course.

clue.text: Fine gold in punt is alongside one not quite loaded

indicators.note: the next pieces are set beside the first one in a row
the symbol for gold goes inside the word for a gamble

parts.note: a punt is a gamble, a bet
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the word for loaded stops just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: loaded means full, filled up

explanation.surface: A gambler's bet in gold sits beside a drinker who isn't quite drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims FULL to FUL; 'punt' is a bet, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and lovely are synonyms when describing something attractive or excellent.

clue.text: Pretend not to have seen undeniable try after injury

indicators.note: after an injury the letters are damaged and reordered

explanation.surface: A rugby referee ignores an undeniable try after a player is hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'after injury' as a rugby moment, a player hurt before the score; it is the anagram signal, and 'undeniable try' is all fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from Nelson's telescope: to deliberately ignore something one has noticed.

clue.text: Manager gets Sinatra and rod Stewart finally playing around Michigan

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the state abbreviation
the letters are played about with, rearranged into a new order
only the closing letter of the singer's surname is used

parts.note: MI is the US postal abbreviation for Michigan

explanation.surface: A manager signs Frank Sinatra and Rod Stewart to perform a gig in Michigan.
explanation.walkthrough: The two singers look like the definition's company, but 'playing' is the anagram signal, and only Stewart's last letter counts; 'Michigan' is a postal code, not a place to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrator runs an organisation's affairs, much as a manager does.

clue.text: Security running side by side

explanation.definitionFit: Assets pledged to guarantee a loan, and an old sense meaning parallel or alongside.

clue.text: Start to use heater — there's one in the hearth

definitions.meaning: heater is old gangster slang for a gun, so starting to use one means beginning to shoot
an uncovered blaze burning in a grate

explanation.surface: Turning on a heater, a householder notes there is a real blaze in the grate too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heater' is American gangster slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: Begin shooting, and also an unenclosed blaze in a domestic fireplace.

clue.text: Sorry excuse

definitions.meaning: said when asking someone to repeat themselves
to forgive or let off an offence

explanation.definitionFit: A polite word asking for repetition, and a verb meaning to forgive.

clue.text: Old revolutionary cracks open beer for dictator

indicators.note: the revolutionary and the old letter break into the beer, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
Che Guevara was the Argentine Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: An old rebel cracks open a beer to toast a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old revolutionary' tempts as one person, but it splits into O and Che Guevara; 'cracks open' is the containment signal, not opening a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusto Pinochet ruled Chile as a military strongman from 1973 to 1990.

clue.text: Trunks held up in the river?

definitions.text: Trunks held up in the river?

parts.words: Trunks held up in the river?
parts.note: the trunks are felled tree timbers, not swimwear, held up by being jammed together in a waterway

explanation.surface: A swimmer's trunks are snagged somewhere in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunks' suggests swimming costume, but it means tree trunks; 'held up' means blocked, not raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangled pile of floating timber blocking a waterway, figuratively any blockage.

clue.text: Howler goes round island with rare creature

indicators.note: the blunder surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a howler is a blunder, a gaffe

explanation.surface: A howling monkey goes round an island with a rare animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Howler' sounds like an animal but means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked African animal is a creature.

clue.text: Short race here — bowler's heard to bet

indicators.note: the bowler's surname is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: Dennis Lillee was a famous Australian fast bowler of the 1970s
to put money on something is to bet it

explanation.surface: A punter bets on a short race, guided by what the cricket bowler says.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis Lillee was an Australian cricket fast bowler; his name 'heard' gives LILLI. 'Short race' is a race of short people, not a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's Gulliver visits this island of tiny people, so a short race lives there.

clue.text: Trouble gay bishop about centrepiece in church

indicators.note: the first letters surround the middle ones

parts.note: in its old sense gay means lively, cheerful, pert
B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: the central letters of the word church are taken

explanation.surface: A gay bishop's view of the church's central feature causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gay' is used in its old sense of lively; PERT and B go 'about' UR, the centre of 'church'.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to disturb or worry them, a synonym of trouble.

clue.text: What driver at t-junction might do next to improve

definitions.text: What driver at t-junction might do next
definitions.meaning: at the top of a T a motorist has to swing left or right round the bend
to get past the worst of an illness or crisis and begin to recover

explanation.surface: A driving instructor explains what to do at a junction to get better.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally steering round a bend; idiomatically starting to recover after a bad spell.

clue.text: Drive out to see the Roman in the river

indicators.note: the article goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
il is Italian for the, the language of modern Rome

explanation.surface: Someone is banished to see a Roman in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile is to banish, drive someone out of their country.

clue.text: Act mirroring part of alphabet ?

parts.note: two consecutive letters of the alphabet

indicators.note: the second copy reflects the first, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the same two consecutive letters again

explanation.surface: An act copying part of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mirroring' sets DE beside its mirror image ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an action performed, a synonym of act.

clue.text: Overhaul broken fire with brush

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A broken fireplace is overhauled with a sweep's brush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges FIRE and BRUSH together.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a building is to renovate or do it up thoroughly.

clue.text: Starters of udo in pickled eel and duck

indicators.note: the picked letters go inside the jumbled ones
pickled, like something drunk or muddled, signals that the letters are jumbled
the opening letters of the word udo are taken, its first two

explanation.surface: A menu of starters: Japanese udo in pickled eel, with duck to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' is plural, so it takes UD, the first two letters of 'udo' (a Japanese vegetable), and puts them 'in' an anagram of EEL. 'duck' is a verb, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or blow is to dodge or evade it.

clue.text: Some food — there's a lot of bits by the river

indicators.note: one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: the Lee is a river in Ireland flowing through Cork (also the Lee or Lea in London)
K stands for kilo, a thousand, as in a kilobit of data

explanation.surface: Someone eats lots of small bits of food beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: K is kilo, a thousand, so a kilobit is 'a lot of bits'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leek is an onion-family vegetable, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Down-and-out here?

parts.note: down means soft feathers used as stuffing, and out means fast asleep, so this is where someone sleeps on stuffed bedding

explanation.surface: A homeless person might sleep rough in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-and-out' looks like a tramp; split it as down (feathers) and out (asleep).
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress stuffed with soft plumage, where a sleeper lies on down.
